blocks.c: It is, I am told, the only one there has ever been, and the whole thing is recorded in the black volume, and the black volume is now a legal document that I am not allowed to take out of the building, which is fine, because it does not want to go.

Mrs. Dalisay came down in the freight car at 06:14 on the twenty-first of March, in a cardigan, with her diary under her arm and her reading glasses on a chain, and she walked up to the counter of an office eleven floors below a basement and said, to a thing that was not a man:
"You have had twenty-two years of my life in boxes and I have written down every single one of them."
She put the diary on the counter.

Every morning since 2003. The name of a night technician she could not picture. A face. A recipe her grandmother taught her. The word for a colour. Four hundred and eleven entries, dated, signed, with a note in the front in her small clear hand: THESE ARE MINE AND I DISPUTE THEIR REMOVAL.
The clerk read the whole thing.
Then it said, "You never got in the elevator."

I have thought since about which of us actually beat that building, and it was not me, and it was not Wen with her thirty-one years on a mop bucket. It was a supervisor who never once went downstairs and never once stopped writing it down.
